last_verified.normal_state: MODEL-RT-01 Nagi 0.2 Model Runtime Foundation acceptance passes on codex/ws-model-runtime. The pinned arm64 host all-target suite passes 40 tests; focused formatting, warnings-denied Clippy, crate check, and nagi doctor pass. The provider-neutral contract covers manifest/runtime and resource classes, capability-aware registry selection, deterministic Standard-to-Lite fallback, generation and streaming, cooperative cancellation, typed failures, health/resource reporting, and a metadata-only System One extension point. No production inference, weights, mandatory network dependency, or M20 implementation is included. CI run 36397861588 caught a CRLF-sensitive assertion in the new optional manifest class compatibility test on Windows. The test now constructs CRLF input and removes the JSON properties independent of line endings; the focused case and all 40 package tests pass after the fix. CI 36398859291 confirms both Ubuntu host and Windows launcher jobs PASS. Its separate Nagi target job is still progressing through the user-init build; target/M17 acceptance is not part of this Foundation criterion. A local Nagi target package check stops in existing libc 0.2.174 declarations missing target_os=nagi types before this crate compiles. Root nagi fmt is blocked by existing Servo format drift; root nagi lint/test fail on existing x86_64 syscall registers under the local arm64 host compiler. Full Draft 2020-12 schema evaluation is deferred under the shared Cargo.lock ownership restriction and is not a Nagi 0.2 Foundation acceptance item. M20 remains NOT STARTED; M17 is independent.

Runtime/backend contracts expose discovery/enumeration, validation, load/unload, invocation, streaming, cooperative cancellation, health, and resource reporting.
Provider-neutral sessions and requests support lifecycle, text/system context, generation options, bounded token usage, timeout, cancellation, and typed errors.

Registry matching checks backend/runtime/class/capability compatibility and deterministically selects configured Granite default, available Standard candidates, and Lite fallback without vendor-specific branches.
Qwen3 4B, IBM Granite 4.2 3B, and Gemma 3 1B are represented by metadata fixtures with Standard/Standard/Lite roles and no model weights.
Deterministic mock-backend tests cover discovery, selection, load/invoke/unload, error paths, streaming, cancellation, health/resource reports, and repeated lifecycle.
System One is an open runtime-class/capability extension point; no System One model, fake inference, DecisionProvider, or jev implementation is claimed.
No model weights, mandatory network dependency, production inference backend, or kernel/runtime hook is introduced.
Focused all-target host tests, package formatting, warnings-denied Clippy, documentation, state, commit, push, and clean branch state are verified.
Production inference and model weights are outside Foundation Acceptance; M20 remains NOT STARTED pending its own milestone criteria.
